stem: Which sentence needs commas?
options / answer: A) We saw lions. | B) Lions roar. | C) We saw lions tigers and bears. | D) We saw lions and tigers.
why correct: Three items in a series need commas: lions, tigers, and bears.
tip: Count the items. Three or more? Use commas.

stem: What does unhappy mean?
options / answer: A) happy again | B) happy before | C) very happy | D) not happy
why correct: The prefix un- means not.
tip: Cover the prefix, read the base word, then add the prefix meaning.

stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
options / answer: A) friend | B) frind | C) freind | D) frend
why correct: Friend is spelled f-r-i-e-n-d.
tip: Memory trick: a friend to the end.

stem: A story about a soccer final is told by the goalkeeper who let in the winning goal. How would the description of the final minute most likely change if the scorer narrated it?
options / answer: A) It would describe the goalkeeper's thoughts in detail. | B) It would focus on excitement and pride instead of disappointment. | C) It would include no feelings at all. | D) It would describe exactly the same feelings.
why correct: A narrator's point of view shapes which feelings and details are emphasized.
tip: RL.5.6: ask how the narrator's experience colors the events.

stem: A text explains that honeybees pollinate crops, that bee numbers are falling, and that farmers are planting wildflower strips to help. Which statement best captures BOTH main ideas?
options / answer: A) Honeybees make honey. | B) Wildflowers are pretty. | C) Bees are essential to farming, and people are acting to reverse their decline. | D) Farmers grow many crops.
why correct: Grade 5 texts can have two main ideas: why bees matter, and how people help them.
tip: Check that your summary statement covers every section.

stem: “The early bird catches the worm.” Which situation shows this proverb?
options / answer: A) A bird ate a worm in the garden. | B) Omar slept late and missed the bus. | C) Lina likes birds more than worms. | D) Noura arrived first at the book sale and found the rarest book.
why correct: The proverb means people who act early get the best opportunities.
tip: Match the proverb's lesson to a real-life example.

stem: Which sentence correctly combines the ideas using a dependent clause? “It was raining. We played inside.”
options / answer: A) Because it was raining, we played inside. | B) It was raining because we played inside. | C) Because it was raining. | D) It was raining, we played inside.
why correct: Because it was raining is a dependent clause that explains why.
tip: Put the cause in the because-clause.

stem: Tap the part of the sentence that has an error.
options / answer: The students forgot | there | notebooks in the library.
why correct: Their shows ownership (the students' notebooks); there tells where.
tip: their = belongs to them; there = place; they're = they are.

skill: Nouns: Common, Proper, Concrete, Abstract, Collective
stem: Which word is a common noun?
options / answer: A) Dammam | B) teacher | C) Ms. Amal | D) Friday
why correct: Teacher names a general person, not a specific one.
tip: Common nouns are not capitalized unless they start a sentence.

stem: What kind of sentence is this? “Please close the window.”
options / answer: A) declarative (a statement) | B) exclamatory (strong feeling) | C) imperative (a command) | D) interrogative (a question)
why correct: Imperative sentences give commands or requests.
tip: Declarative . | Interrogative ? | Exclamatory ! | Imperative (command).

stem: Which word is a synonym for begin?
options / answer: A) pause | B) finish | C) forget | D) start
why correct: Begin and start mean the same thing.
tip: Swap the words in a sentence: if the meaning stays, they're synonyms.

skill: Adjectives, Articles and Order of Adjectives
stem: Which word is an adjective? “A tall building shone brightly.”
options / answer: A) tall | B) building | C) shone | D) brightly
why correct: Tall describes what kind of building.
tip: Adjectives answer: what kind? which one? how many?

stem: Which word is more formal than kids?
options / answer: A) folks | B) children | C) guys | D) buddies
why correct: Children is the formal, standard word.
tip: Use formal words in reports and essays.

stem: Which claim would require the strongest evidence to be convincing?
options / answer: A) Many teachers assign reading homework. | B) Some students prefer homework on weekends. | C) Homework has no effect on student learning at any grade level. | D) Homework can help students practise skills.
why correct: Absolute claims (“no effect,” “any grade”) need broad, strong evidence because one counterexample can disprove them.
tip: The bigger the claim, the stronger the evidence it needs.

stem: In a story, a girl lies to protect her friend; the lie grows, the friendship nearly breaks, and she finally confesses. The friend forgives her. Which theme is developed MOST fully?
options / answer: A) Protecting friends is more important than anything. | B) Friends should never forgive each other. | C) Lying always works out in the end. | D) Honesty, even when difficult, is necessary for trust between friends.
why correct: The plot moves from a lie, to consequences, to a confession that restores trust.
tip: RL.6.2: track how the theme develops through particular details.

stem: A writer wants readers to admire a character who rarely gives up. Which word should the writer choose?
options / answer: A) determined | B) inflexible | C) stubborn | D) pigheaded
why correct: Determined has a positive connotation for not giving up.
tip: Choose words whose feeling matches your purpose.

stem: Tap the part of the sentence that has an error.
options / answer: Between you and | I, | the test was easy.
why correct: Between is a preposition, so it takes the objective case: between you and me.
tip: After prepositions (between, for, with, to), use me, him, her, us, them.

stem: Which sentence correctly uses parentheses to set off nonessential information?
options / answer: A) The museum open (since 1985) attracts, thousands of visitors. | B) The museum (open since 1985) attracts thousands of visitors. | C) The museum (open since 1985 attracts) thousands of visitors. | D) The (museum open since 1985) attracts thousands of visitors.
why correct: Parentheses go around extra information that could be removed without breaking the sentence.
tip: Read the sentence without the parentheses—it should still make sense.
